title.narrative: EA 12/2010 Emergency Preparedness and Rapid Response Capacity: Dioceses of Yei and Tombura-Yambio

description.narrative:
The aim of this project is to strengthen the capacity of the Caritas family (diocese, national, and member organisations) in Sudan to respond to anticipated emergency situations in the country, including any scenarios that develop during the build up and aftermath of the Referenda as well as other man made or natural disasters. The overall goal is; To strengthen Church and community structures to mitigate the impact of humanitarian disasters in Sudan. This intervention will focus on the 2 dioceses of Tombura-Yambio and Yei in Sudan with the following specific objective; The 2 Dioceses will develop effective emergency preparedness plans and have the capacity to deliver the responses in their target communities. The expected results are ; Diocesan and Caritas agencies staff strengthen their skills and knowledge in emergency preparedness and response, Communities in each diocese are prepared to respond to emergencies or disasters, Increased institutional capacity of Diocesan, Sudanaid and other Caritas members to respond to emerging humanitarian needs, Establish a Parish Based Information Systems in all 9 Dioceses in Sudan. The direct beneficiaries of the project is the planned 25 staff each from the diocese of Tombura-Yambio and Yei to be trained on emergency preparedness and response, additional 2 emergency coordinators to be recruited per diocese. CAFOD staff shall provide minimum capacity within the 2 dioceses and focused on likely hotspots, to enable them to respond effectively to any emergencies that may arise. Communities in the 2 dioceses will also benefit through participation in emergency preparedness and early response activities. These beneficiaries will be reached through activities such as community managed disaster preparedness.
This contribution from CRS will be targeted to the Dioceses of Yei and Tombura-Yambio and will fund the salary of the 2 Diocese Emergency Coordinators for 1 year, as well as fund the EPR, EPP and CMDRR trainings, and purchase of communication/information systems. There are flexible funds for other urgent activities identified through the Emergency Preparedness Plans.
